item.title: 'Passport has discrepancies in place of birth': Saurav Das rendered ineligible for foreign travel
item.description: CJP activist Saurav Das has been served a notice by the Regional Passport Office regarding his birth documents. The notice requires him to respond within seven days to clarify discrepancies in his documents. If he fails to provide a satisfactory explanation, his passport may be impounded under the Passports Act. A pending re-verification will determine his eligibility for international travel once cleared.
item.dc:creator: Bharti Jain

item.title: 1st privately built PSLV set for launch early next year: Isro chief
item.description: Isro Chairman V Narayanan announced the first privately built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle is ready for launch. This PSLV-N1 rocket is being developed by a consortium including L&T and HAL. The government is promoting satellite launches in collaboration with startups, which have increased to over 440. Narayanan emphasized the importance of building more space assets for communication and navigation.
item.dc:creator: Surendra Singh

item.title: Rajiv Gandhi's security withdrawn to get him killed, says Rahul
item.description: In a recent family conversation about Sonia Gandhi's latest book, Rahul Gandhi accused the government of intentionally removing his father Rajiv Gandhi's security, suggesting it fostered the conditions for his assassination. Following his exit from office in 1989, Rajiv's protection was significantly reduced. Furthermore, Rahul is poised to address the political victimization and humiliation Sonia endured during her career.

item.title: Amit Shah: Kartarpur corridor to open after review
item.description: Union home minister Amit Shah expressed that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor will only reopen after addressing prevailing security issues. This corridor, which offers hassle-free access for pilgrims, was shut down following security alerts linked to Operation Sindoor. Shah highlighted the need to keep national security discussions free from political influences, while also pointing out that the corridor's placement in Pakistan stemmed from Congress party oversights during partition.

item.title: NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet
item.description: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Maldives defense minister Hassan Rasheed discussed security cooperation at the Colombo Security Conclave. This meeting marked the first high-level interaction between the two countries since President Mohamed Muizzu's recent visit to Pakistan. During that visit, Maldives signed 20 agreements with Pakistan related to defense and maritime issues. Additionally, Muizzu called for resuming the Saarc summit process to enhance regional cooperation.

item.title: PM Modi, Merz say India-EU FTA will unlock new opportunities
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently engaged in discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, focused on enhancing the India-Germany Strategic Partnership. The conversation covered various critical areas including trade, investment, defence, and cutting-edge technologies, underscoring both nations’ dedication to global peace. As they commemorate 75 years of diplomatic ties, they aim to bolster cooperation across essential sectors while sharing insights on regional issues of common interest.

item.title: From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art
item.description: The CII Banaras Biennale is set to commence on November 27, culminating on December 31. This unique event aims to intertwine the ancient and modern art scenes, presenting the vibrant culture of Banaras. Activities will unfold at numerous venues, including the distinguished Bharatiya Kala Bhavan. By fostering partnerships between cultural institutions and industry, the Biennale aspires to spark rich dialogues, bridging diverse artistic expressions with their historical narratives.
item.dc:creator: Neelam Raaj

item.title: Government may link motor insurance premiums to traffic violations
item.description: The road transport ministry is gearing up to introduce initiatives to lower the incidence of uninsured vehicles on Indian roads. Key proposals include establishing a unified insurance premium for different vehicle types. Furthermore, traffic violations recorded against vehicle owners could potentially affect their insurance costs. A trial of the 'no insurance, no fuel' strategy will be initiated at select fuel stations.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash

item.title: Dalai Lama, office allotted bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi
item.description: The Centre has assigned a government bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama. This official accommodation aims to facilitate his visits to the national capital and provide comfort. Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile have welcomed this arrangement as a supportive gesture towards their community. Gaden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama's office, was registered as a private trust in India in 2011.

item.title: BSF constable dies by suicide in Arnia
item.description: In a tragic incident, Deva Nand Majhi, a young BSF constable stationed in Jammu and Kashmir, reportedly took his own life at a security camp. The shocking event unfolded in the Arnia border region late Monday night when he allegedly utilized his service weapon. Originally from Katsa in Bihar's Saran district, his remains have been sent to GMC Jammu's mortuary for autopsy.
item.dc:creator: Sanjay Khajuria

item.title: Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row
item.description: Concerns are mounting among political leaders, notably PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, regarding the construction activities near Sheshnag Lake. Environmental advocates and Congress members underscore the area's ecological sensitivity. The Border Roads Organisation defends its initiatives as critical for ensuring safety for pilgrims on the Amarnath Yatra route. Detractors warn that development could endanger local ecosystems, revealing a broader conflict between aspirations for growth and the need for environmental conservation.
item.dc:creator: Naseer Ganai and Sanjay Khajuria

item.title: Rijiju heaps praise on J&K Waqf Board led by BJP man
item.description: Union minister Kiren Rijiju praised the Jammu & Kashmir Waqf Board for its remarkable contributions across various sectors, particularly citing the development projects at the Hazratbal and Baba Reshi shrines. Rijiju remarked that this waqf board serves as a role model for similar entities nationwide. He also pledged to aid in skill development and training programs aimed at empowering the youth of Kashmir.

item.title: Indians among 13 killed in UAE bus-truck crash, 14 injured
item.description: In a heartbreaking incident in Ras Al Khaimah, thirteen lives were tragically lost, including several Indian nationals, as confirmed by the Indian consulate in Dubai. A bus with 41 passengers collided with a parked truck, resulting in this devastating accident. Emergency teams quickly responded, transporting the injured to local hospitals for care. The consulate has established a helpline for those seeking further information and support regarding this unfortunate event.
